_comment: ngsolve contact#0 (penalty gamma too small -> contact not enforced; too large -> ill-conditioning). Run 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604: unit-square elastic block E=1000 nu=0.3 fixed on top, body force 150 pressing it onto a rigid floor 0.01 below its bottom edge, penalty energy 0.5*gamma*<-(u_y+G0)>_+^2 on the bottom edge through ngsolve.solvers.Newton, maxh 0.2. The small-gamma half of the claim holds: penetration is 27.7% of an element edge at gamma=10 and falls monotonically to under 5% by gamma=1e4, so the claim's 5% observable discriminates. CORRECTION to the large-gamma half: the messages the claim names are never emitted. At gamma=1e22, with stdout and stderr captured, there is no DivisionByZero, no NewtonMinimization and no condition-number warning; what happens is that Newton stops converging, returns status -1 after consuming all 40 iterations, and says so in different words -- 'Warning: Newton might not converge! Error = '. An agent grepping the claimed strings finds nothing and reads the solve as clean. The fixture also confirms the return tuple is (status, numit) with status first, against solvers.Newton's own docstring. Mutation: capping the gamma sweep at 1e3 removes the tight end and the fixture fails on high_gamma_penetration_under_5pct_of_edge.
